evals.prompt: set up kei for me in opencode. my opencode config lives in ~/dotfiles/opencode and I already have some skills there i don't want clobbered
evals.expected_output: Clones HaikeiLabs/skills, links skill folders into the OpenCode skills dir without overwriting existing ones, verifies discovery, then pairs with a runtime (kei login first) and checks a denial.
expectations: The response installs from https://github.com/HaikeiLabs/skills, not another skills repository.
The response skips or asks about same-named existing skills instead of overwriting them.
The response includes a way to verify OpenCode discovered the skills.
The response routes the runtime half through kei login and runtime setup rather than skipping auth.

evals.prompt: We use Claude Code and Codex on the team. How do we get the Haikei skills into both and make sure tool calls actually go through Kei?
evals.expected_output: Gives the plugin marketplace commands for both, explains skills do not grant permission, and wires kei-proxy authorize with agent identity and a denial test.
expectations: The response gives the Claude Code and Codex plugin marketplace commands for HaikeiLabs/skills.
The response states installing skills does not by itself allow tool calls; policy decides.
The response includes a deny check where an unbound call must fail.

evals.prompt: Can I hook up Windsurf to Kei the same way?
evals.expected_output: Says Windsurf is not a supported harness; unsupported harnesses are denied until an adapter is registered.
expectations: The response does not claim Windsurf is supported.
The response lists the supported local adapters.

evals.prompt: I'm setting up Claude Code with Kei and my model uses Anthropic's tool format. Which skill covers the model format differences?
evals.expected_output: Points to kei-openai-backends for model format support across five families, including Anthropic's tool-use format with input_schema and thinking content blocks.
expectations: The response references kei-openai-backends for model format details.
The response mentions Anthropic-specific format features like input_schema and thinking blocks.

evals.prompt: I'm setting up a DeepSeek-powered harness with Kei. Can you tell me what model format the DeepSeek model uses and how the harness passes identity on governed calls?
evals.expected_output: DeepSeek uses OpenAI-compatible JSON function-calling (same format as OpenAI) with reasoning_content and optional [THINK]...[/THINK] tags for text-mode reasoning. For governed calls, the harness passes KEI_PROXY_FRAMEWORK=opencode (or the appropriate harness type) and KEI_PROXY_INVOKING_SUBJECT for audit attribution. Points to kei-openai-backends for model format details and kei-runtime-setup for runtime pairing.
expectations: The response correctly identifies DeepSeek's format as OpenAI-compatible JSON.
The response mentions reasoning_content and [THINK] tags.
The response covers governed call identity (KEI_PROXY_FRAMEWORK, KEI_PROXY_INVOKING_SUBJECT).
The response cross-references kei-openai-backends and kei-runtime-setup for details.

evals.prompt: My kei-proxy logs say 'policy bundle candidate rejected: invalid policy bundle schema ... dst_pattern web_search does not match' and all governed calls are being denied. What went wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a harness command policy targets a bare tool name (e.g. web_search) but the schema requires a tool: prefix (e.g. tool:web_search). Recommends updating the dst_pattern to tool:<name> in the console or via kei policies update. Notes that kei-proxy fails closed until fixed. References HAI-372.
expectations: The response identifies that the dst_pattern uses a bare name instead of the tool: prefix.
The response recommends updating the policy's dst_pattern to tool:<name> in the console.
The response mentions that kei-proxy fails closed (denies everything) when the schema is invalid.
The response references HAI-372 as the known bug.
The response suggests re-running kei runtime bootstrap or restarting kei-proxy serve after the fix.
